summary: Tested HeartLink Smart Welcome Message system (TEST 1-10). Backend: 14 pytest tests written+run against public URL (welcome-check new/returning/active/unknown user, welcome-shown, welcome-clicked, admin GET/PUT welcome-settings incl. disable + message editing + analytics counters) — all passed (100%). Frontend: new-user WelcomeModal renders correctly with all required testids, CTA closes modal + tracks click, admin Settings tab shows full Welcome Messages section with toggles/editors/analytics/Save (save works, toast shown). TWO major bugs found: (1) welcome_back never fires in the real login flow because /api/auth/login updates last_active=now before the frontend calls welcome-check (verified in UI: welcome-check returned show:false for a 9-day-inactive user right after login); (2) admin welcome message text inputs lose focus after every keystroke (only 1 char registers) because Toggle/TextInput/TextArea are declared inline inside WelcomeSettings.

minor.issue: No authentication/authorization — reachable with a plain unauthenticated session (no JWT / X-Admin-Id). Any anonymous caller can read or rewrite global welcome messages.
Unknown/invalid user_id returns 200 {show:false} instead of 404 (acceptable but hides bad IDs).

ui_bugs.issue: Toggle/TextInput/TextArea are defined as inline components inside WelcomeSettings, so they are remounted on every state change. Typing loses focus after each character — typing 'HELLO QA' resulted in value 'Welcome to HeartLinkH' and document.activeElement became null. Admin effectively cannot edit welcome titles/messages/CTAs. Fix: move Toggle/TextInput/TextArea outside the component (module scope) and pass value/onChange as props.

integration_issues.flow: Returning user (7+ days inactive) welcome-back on login
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL: /api/auth/login sets users.last_active = now (server.py ~line 1389-1396) before the frontend calls GET /api/welcome-check/{id} (App.js checkWelcome, 800ms after login). days_inactive is therefore always 0 and welcome-check returns {show:false}. Reproduced in UI with review@heartlink.co.in seeded to last_active=9 days ago + welcome_back_shown_at unset — no modal, network response {"show":false}. Feature works only when queried before login (curl/pytest). Fix: persist previous_last_active on login (or return welcome eligibility from the login response / compute welcome server-side inside the login handler).

integration_issues.flow: Welcome modal vs Daily Reward modal
integration_issues.issue: In App.js handleLogin the daily-reward timer checks `if (!welcomeData)` inside setTimeout — that reads the stale closure value (always null at handleLogin time), so the guard never works. Observed daily reward modal appearing immediately after the welcome CTA; with slower networks it can stack on top of the welcome modal. Use a ref or chain daily reward off welcome dismissal.

issues: Settings panel content overflows horizontally: section headings ('Feature Settings', 'Welcome Messages') render flush at x=0 with no left padding and the pink 'Save Changes' button is clipped at the right viewport edge.
Welcome Messages 'Save Changes' button sits far from the editors it saves; consider sticky/bottom placement.

action_items: Fix welcome_back: store previous last_active (e.g. prev_last_active) before /api/auth/login overwrites it, and use it in check_welcome_message — otherwise the returning-user welcome is dead code in production.
Move Toggle/TextInput/TextArea out of the WelcomeSettings component body to stop input remount/focus loss (admin cannot type messages today).
Replace stale-closure `if (!welcomeData)` daily-reward guard in App.js handleLogin with a ref or sequential trigger.
Add admin auth (JWT/X-Admin-Id middleware, as used by other /api/admin routes) to GET/PUT /api/admin/welcome-settings.
Fix admin Settings panel horizontal overflow / clipped Save button on desktop.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 8351 lines — welcome system should live in its own router module.
check_welcome_message swallows all exceptions in the returning-user branch (bare except: pass), which will silently hide date-parsing bugs.
PUT /api/admin/welcome-settings takes a raw request body with a manual allow-list instead of a Pydantic model; returning_inactivity_days is not range-validated (any int/type accepted).
welcome-shown / welcome-clicked accept any user_id without verifying the user exists and without auth, so analytics counters can be inflated by anyone.

success_rate.frontend: 70% (new-user modal + admin section render/save OK; welcome-back flow and message editing broken)

seed_data_creation: Created 4 temporary TEST_ users directly in Mongo (deleted in teardown, verified 0 remaining). Reset then restored welcome fields for review@heartlink.co.in (currently welcome_shown_at=40d ago, last_active=9d ago from seeding — login will have refreshed last_active). Admin welcome settings were mutated during tests and restored to defaults (verified new_user_title='Welcome to HeartLink', both toggles true).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_welcome_iter32.py (pytest, seeds its own users via pymongo, restores admin settings). Correct login route is /api/auth/login (not /api/login). To retest welcome-back in the UI you must fix the last_active overwrite first; UI verification = login as review user with last_active 8+ days old and assert [data-testid='welcome-modal'] with type welcome_back. Admin welcome editors: verify typing multiple characters into [data-testid='welcome-input-new_user_title'] persists (focus-loss bug).
rca_of_the_issue: Welcome-back RCA: the login handler (server.py ~1389) does db.users.update_one({...},{'$set':{...,'last_active': now}}) as part of successful auth. The frontend only calls GET /api/welcome-check/{id} 800ms after that, so (now - last_active).days == 0 < returning_inactivity_days and the endpoint returns {show:false}. Admin editor RCA: WelcomeSettings.jsx defines Toggle/TextInput/TextArea as function components inside the parent render; each setSettings creates new component identities, React unmounts/remounts the DOM input, and the caret/focus is lost after the first character.
